explanation: Son of Abraham and Sarah, who is an important patriarch in the Jewish, Christian, and Islamic tradition.
Wife of Isaac and mother to the twins Esau and Jacob.
Eldest son of Isaac and Rebekah, known for selling his birthright to his brother Jacob for a bowl of lentil stew.
Younger twin brother of Esau, who with the help of his mother Rebekah deceived his older brother and received the birthright and blessing from his father Isaac.
A right given to the firstborn son in a family, which included inheritance of the family's property and status as head of the family.
A divine favor or protection, often given by God through a patriarch such as Isaac.
